meta.title: Project | Green Ecolution | Smart Green Space Management
meta.description: Green Ecolution is an open-source solution for efficient irrigation of urban trees, developed in collaboration with the City of Flensburg.

hero.label: Project
hero.headline: Smart green space management for livable cities
hero.description: Green Ecolution is an open-source solution for the efficient irrigation of urban trees. Our software combines sensor data with intelligent route optimization, enabling targeted, resource-efficient deployment planning. Developed in collaboration with the City of Flensburg, and soon available for your municipality too.

dashboard.description: Our system scientifically evaluates the sensor data and shows when irrigation is needed. The data is prepared so that it is easy to interpret and can be directly incorporated into deployment planning.
dashboard.imageAlt: Green Ecolution dashboard - overview of irrigation recommendations

process.title: Measure. Understand. Act.
process.description: From soil moisture to an optimized irrigation route, in one continuous digital workflow.

measure.title: Measure
measure.description: Soil moisture sensors capture parameters such as soil moisture, temperature, and soil water tension at multiple depths (30/60/90 cm). The data is transmitted energy-efficiently via LoRaWAN.

details.item1: Soil moisture sensors at depths of 30, 60, and 90 cm
details.item2: Measurement of soil moisture, temperature, and soil water tension
details.item4: Flush-mounted installation, no impact on maintenance work

understand.title: Understand
understand.description: A traffic-light system shows the current irrigation need on a map. Staff can see at a glance which green spaces need water. Time series enable detailed analyses.

details.item1: Traffic-light system shows irrigation needs on a map
details.item2: Prioritization by urgency when capacity is limited
details.item3: Time series for soil moisture, temperature, and water tension
details.item4: Real-time dashboard with all relevant KPIs

act.title: Act
act.description: Automated dispatch and route planning generates optimized irrigation routes, taking into account water capacity, vehicle size, and road restrictions.

details.item2: Takes water capacity and vehicle size into account
details.item4: Export of routes to navigation devices

architecture.title: The path of the data
architecture.description: This is how the readings travel from the tree to the optimized irrigation route through the Green Ecolution system.
architecture.streamletRich: Route optimisation in the backend is handled by <streamlet>Streamlet</streamlet>, a separate open source project that can also be used outside Green Ecolution.

sensor.label: Sensor
sensor.description: Measures soil moisture at the tree

requirements.title: What you need for it
requirements.lead: Getting started is smaller than it first looks. The four points describe what has to come from the municipality.
requirements.sensorsOptionalNote: Scheduling and route planning already work without sensors. Trees, fleet and refill points are enough. The soil probes improve the prioritisation because they show which areas actually need water.

treeData.label: Tree and area data
treeData.description: Locations come in via CSV import or by connecting an existing tree register. There is no need to build a register from scratch.

fleet.label: The fleet you already have
fleet.description: Water carts, vans and trailers with their water capacities, plus the refill points across the city. A new fleet or fixed irrigation hardware is not required.

network.label: LoRaWAN coverage once sensors are added
network.description: The probes transmit over the open The Things Network. Since 2024 Schleswig-Holstein has built a state-wide network with more than 420 gateways. Only outside such coverage does a gateway of your own become necessary.

hosting.label: Somewhere to run it
hosting.description: The platform runs in a Kubernetes cluster, either in your own or the municipality's infrastructure, or hosted. The software itself is free of licence fees.

requirements.tourLinkRich: How the route optimisation works and what input it expects is described on the <streamlet>route optimisation</streamlet> page.

productScope.title: What the system consists of
productScope.description: Green Ecolution consists of software, hardware and the services around them. The software is open source; the probes and the support come from PROGEEK GmbH in Flensburg.
productScope.framing: The master's project at Flensburg University of Applied Sciences showed that the approach holds up in municipal day-to-day work. What municipalities get today is built on that foundation at PROGEEK.

software.label: Software
software.description: The platform with its map and dashboard, grouping into irrigation units, fleet and team management, the user and role model, route optimisation with refill stations, the mobile app and the review of consumption. The source code is open and there are no licence fees for municipalities.

hardware.label: Hardware
hardware.description: The soil probe records the soil water status at several depths and transmits over LoRaWAN. It is designed for public spaces, is installed flush with the ground using standard earth augers and does not get in the way of maintenance work such as mowing. The probes are available through PROGEEK, a firmware of our own is in development, and regional manufacturing is the goal going forward.

services.label: Services
services.description: PROGEEK handles hosting and operation, adapts the platform to the municipality's organisational structure, connects existing data sources and supports the rollout. Anyone who prefers to run it themselves can do that just as well.

governance.title: Open source as a principle
governance.description: Transparency, independence, and reusability: the cornerstones of our open-source strategy.

license.title: AGPL-3.0-only
license.description: Licensed under the AGPL. Funded as part of DigitalHub.SH's "Offene Innovation" ("Open Innovation") state program.

sovereignty.title: Digital sovereignty
sovereignty.description: No dependency on proprietary platforms. Municipalities retain control over their data and infrastructure. No vendor lock-in.

modularity.title: Plugin system
modularity.description: Modular extensions for municipality-specific adaptations without changing the core software. Import plugins for tree registries, CSV, and databases.

integration.title: API-first
integration.description: Open interfaces for integration into municipal IT landscapes. Connection to IoT hubs and open data portals.

community.title: Reuse & community
community.description: Source code and documentation are publicly available on GitHub. Other municipalities can reuse and adapt the solution.

costEfficiency.title: Cost efficiency
costEfficiency.description: No licence fees for municipalities. Value creation stays in Schleswig-Holstein because development and operation happen regionally.

advantages.title: All other features and advantages
advantages.description: The project is publicly viewable and aims to reduce water consumption for irrigation while enabling variable deployment planning.

openSource.title: An open solution for everyone
openSource.description: Scalable open-source solution for municipalities that promotes further development and transparency

optimizedRoutes.title: Optimized routes
optimizedRoutes.description: Individual deployment planning for more efficient irrigation

vision.title: Made for every municipality
vision.descriptionPart1: The platform is deliberately designed to be usable in any municipality. Map areas, organizational structures, and irrigation regions are freely configurable.
vision.descriptionPart2: Only open standards and open-source components are used. A cloud-native architecture based on Kubernetes enables multi-tenant, highly available operation. Additional municipalities can easily be added.

mediaFeature.title: Green Ecolution on the Schleswig-Holstein Magazin
mediaFeature.description: In August 2026 public broadcaster NDR reported on urban trees that no longer survive the dry summers and spent a morning filming in Flensburg. The piece shows a soil moisture sensor going into the ground and how the city's technical operations centre plans the next watering run from its readings.
mediaFeature.posterAlt: View up into an oak canopy with the sun flaring through the leaves, the Schleswig-Holstein Magazin logo in the bottom left corner
